$comment: SUBSYSTEM PATH REGISTRATION REQUEST from the journeys wave (corpus/88-journeys/ and corpus/85-platform/). subsystems.json is the canonical, append-only taxonomy and is owned by CRT (critic doctrine); an agent outside CRT must not edit it silently. This file is therefore the formal request: every path listed under `new_paths` appears in the `judges:` front-matter of a reference item written in this wave and is currently an ORPHAN under CORPUS-CONTRACT §4 / subsystems.json $comment. Until CRT appends these entries to subsystems.json and regenerates INDEX.md via tools/corpus-index.mjs, tools/corpus-index.mjs will report them in its orphan list. The entries below are pre-formatted in subsystems.json's exact record shape ({path,title,arb,area,critic}) so registration is a copy, not a rewrite.

new_roots.rationale: A journey path judges an END-TO-END PLAYER SEQUENCE, not a subsystem. It is deliberately a separate root because its failures are compositional: every subsystem in the chain can pass its own item while the journey through them fails. journey.* items are the only place the corpus scores the seams BETWEEN subsystems, and giving them a root of their own makes that gap visible in INDEX.md rather than hiding it inside whichever subsystem happened to be nearest.
new_roots.note: A journey path MUST NOT duplicate a subsystem path's bar. Where a journey item needs a subsystem's number it cites the owning item; the division of labour is stated in the blockquote at the top of every RI-JRN*.

new_roots.rationale: Input existed only as `platform.input.pipeline` — one path covering the whole of binding, translation, discoverability and device lifecycle. That is far too coarse to score: a build can have a flawless 60 Hz latched input pipeline and still be unplayable because parry is unbound on a gamepad. `platform.input.pipeline` is retained and keeps its original meaning (the timing/latching pipeline). The `input.*` root owns the CONTRACT the pipeline carries: which actions exist, how devices reach them, and whether a player can find them.
new_roots.note: input.* is device-facing and cross-cutting. It is not a combat root: combat.input.buffer keeps ownership of buffering windows and is not moved here.

new_paths.title: First launch to first meaningful choice as one unbroken act
Character creation happens inside the fiction, not in a settings menu
How much the game explains, and whether it is said by a person in the world
The first hour judged by what the hands do, not by what the story says
The point at which a new player becomes measurably competent, and that it arrives
Save, load, and an empty state diff — end to end, mid-quest, mid-dungeon
new_paths.note: Correctness is binary. arb is neutral because neither reference game rules on browser persistence; the item defines the bar outright.

new_paths.title: Die, lose souls, respawn, run back, recover the bloodstain, as one measured sequence
new_paths.note: Judged under seam S6 (ARBITRATION.md): the loss loop is Souls, the persistence of quest/journal/faction state across death is Morrowind. combat.death.corpserun and combat.death.worldreset keep ownership of the rules; this path owns the end-to-end run.

new_paths.title: A quest completed end to end with no markers, using in-game text alone
A returning player rebuilds their own objectives from in-game information alone
The closed Souls action set exists, is complete, and is reachable on every device
new_paths.note: The 14 action names are fixed by HARNESS.md §4 and may not be extended without a harness amendment.

new_paths.title: Pointer lock acquisition, loss, recovery, and what the game does while unlocked
Physical-key (`code`) binding, layout independence, ghosting, modifier and focus hazards
Rebinding: coverage, conflict handling, persistence, and reset
Whether a player who was told nothing can find each action
new_paths.note: Scored primarily by the naive-agent pass (JOURNEY-CRITIC-FLEET.md §4). The instrumented pass cannot measure this at all — an agent that has read the corpus already knows the binding.

new_paths.title: Every action and every UI surface is reachable on keyboard+mouse, gamepad, and touch
Gamepad button map for the Souls action set, across standard and non-standard descriptors
Deadzones, stick response curves, and analog trigger thresholds with hysteresis
Connect, hot-plug, disconnect mid-combat, resume, and held-input release
The no-gamepad touch path on a phone, and that it is not a second-class game
Landscape lock, safe areas, browser-chrome collapse, DPR, and orientation change
The storage-backend ruling: IndexedDB authoritative, file export mandatory, quota and eviction
new_paths.note: Distinct from platform.save.persistence, which owns WHAT survives. This path owns WHERE it lives and what happens when the browser takes it away.

new_paths.title: CPU cost of one fixed simulation step, measured with rendering disabled
new_paths.note: Separated from platform.perf.framerate because it is measurable on a software rasteriser and frame rate is not (RI-PLT01 §A, Tier-S vs Tier-H).

new_paths.title: Bytes allocated per simulation step and GC attribution to the sim loop
new_paths.note: Per-frame allocation. Session-scale heap growth is platform.perf.memory and belongs to RI-PLT02; the two failures have different causes and are deliberately separate paths.

new_paths.title: Texture, geometry, audio and download budgets for a mid-range phone
Time to first playable frame, and the cost of every subsequent load boundary
new_paths.note: RI-JRN01 O5 (`T_control`) resolves here and is not redefined there.

new_paths.title: Hitch count and duration per traversal minute, and what counts as a declared load boundary
new_paths.note: RI-PLT01 M12 (no frame over 100 ms) excludes declared load boundaries; this path owns the definition of that exclusion, so the two items cannot each assume the other bounds it.

new_critics.description: Judges end-to-end player journeys: the opening, the first hour, controls on every device, save/load, death and recovery, an unmarked quest, and re-entry after a week. Runs as a FLEET of one critic per journey with fresh context (JOURNEY-CRITIC-FLEET.md), and half of its roles are NAIVE agents that have not read the corpus. Never judges a subsystem in isolation — that is the owning critic's job — and never accepts a passing subsystem as evidence that the journey through it works.
new_critics.note: The remaining journey items are assigned to existing critics (critic.ui, critic.platform, critic.combat, critic.quests, critic.journal) so that the fleet does not become a parallel critic hierarchy. Only RI-JRN01 needs a critic that no existing role covers.

harness_amendments_requested.note: Not subsystem paths, listed here so registration and harness amendment are visible in one place. The full, normative request — signatures, semantics, and which items are unmeasurable without each — is JOURNEY-CRITIC-FLEET.md §7. HARNESS.md §10 is the amendment procedure.
